audit.recode_to: Re-enter (or at minimum re-reason) on Kurebito 2004:141-142 + Zhukova 1972:40-41: disyllables initial; longer words stress the 2nd syllable and every second syllable thereafter, never the final — beat strings stress placement coded per word length as 10 010 0100 01010 010100 0101010 01010100 (1 = a stressed syllable) — with fences: (a) schwa-sensitive shifts (initial ə -> 01 in disyllables; 2nd-syllable ə -> retraction to 1st), (b) neither source ranks primary vs secondary (Kurebito marks all beats alike; Zhukova 'весьма условно'), (c) Kurebito's data are mainland (Severo-Evensk) Chawchuvan. If the catalog's scope test requires a unique PRIMARY at every length, keep OUT but change the reason from 'sources-undetermined' to 'rhythmic peninitial-nonfinal, primary undesignated, vowel-quality-sensitive (Kurebito 2004:142)'. Either way the StressTyp2 string second stress stays refuted at n=2 (both sources: initial) and at n>=5 (iterative beats, not a single peninitial).
audit.reasoning: Quote check: the record carries no quotation, but the deciding pages (Zhukova 1972 §41, pp.40-41) are held as a full scan plus 300-dpi page images and every phrase the editor note relies on is verbatim there; the StressTyp2-contradiction note is also correct (no peninitial statement on those pages; Gordon 2002:494 cites Zhukova 1972 for it). Deciding source: the standard 1972 reference grammar, whose stress paragraph is explicitly provisional. Best available: NO before today — Kurebito 2004 'A Report on Koryak Phonology' (ELPR A2-043, open access at TUFS) was unknown to the record and to the 2026-08-18 lit review; downloaded, scanned (no text layer, 250 dpi, sequential tesseract) and read from page images. Its §4.3 states a determinate rule: disyllables initial; >2 syllables 'stress falls on every second syllable, starting from the second syllable, excluding the final syllable', with schwa-conditione
